summary: Put the standalone ?view=map window behind MAP_WINDOW_ENABLED = false, one increment ahead of deleting it in D6.

coordination.notes: A1 is [x], so App.tsx is Lane D's per the section 3 conflict matrix. The flag gates the existing branch in view(); it does not add a parallel router.

checks: Finding recorded rather than assumed: nothing in src/ opens ?view=map. `grep -rn "view=map" src/ src-tauri/ tools/` found only App.tsx's own doc comment and two tool files naming the route in prose. MapPanel's pop-out button calls openPanelWindow('map', 'Map'), which is the generic panel window (?view=panel&id=map) and is untouched by this flag. The gated branch was reachable only by typing the query string, so this increment closes a door that had already lost its handle - which is also why D6's deletion is smaller than it looks.

D3 verify as written (`grep -rn "view=map" src/ | grep -v MAP_WINDOW_ENABLED` -> empty) passes, but its positive control fails: `grep -rc "view=map" src/App.tsx` -> 0. Rewording the doc comment removed the last occurrence of that literal from src/, so the verify grep now has nothing to find and would pass just as readily if the branch were still ungated. Recorded rather than quietly accepted, and re-run against the thing that actually decides behaviour:

`grep -rn "'view') === 'map'" src/` -> one hit, `src/App.tsx:85:  if (MAP_WINDOW_ENABLED && q.get('view') === 'map') return { kind: 'map' }`. The same grep filtered through `grep -v MAP_WINDOW_ENABLED` -> empty. So the branch exists, there is exactly one of it, and it is gated.
